criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001a: Identifies 24-month lookback deviation in service standard
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly identifies that draft Section 3.1 uses a 24-month lookback instead of the APA-required 12-month lookback and revises the provision to use the twelve months immediately preceding closing. The review memo also flags this as a critical must-change issue.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001b: Identifies 'or better than' qualifier in service standard
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags Section 3.1's “at least equal to or better than” language as an upward-ratcheting standard that conflicts with the APA’s “substantially consistent” benchmark, and replaces it with that narrower standard while stating Polaris need not exceed historical quality, timeliness, or responsiveness.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001c: Identifies undefined 'industry best practices' benchmark
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags the draft’s “industry best practices” requirement as an undefined, external, potentially expansive standard not supported by the APA. It deletes that requirement from Section 3.1 and recommends a 12-month, historically based “substantially consistent” standard with “no best-practices overlay.”

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001d: Proposes redline conforming service standard to playbook
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 3.1 includes corrective replacement language requiring each Service to be provided “in a manner substantially consistent with the manner and level of quality” at which it was provided to the Business during the twelve months immediately preceding Closing, which conforms to the playbook standard.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002a: Identifies liability cap as 200% of total fees vs. APA's trailing 12-month cap
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly identifies that draft Section 10.1 uses a cap equal to 200% of total Service Charges paid and contrasts it with APA Section 7.12(d), which requires a cap based on fees actually paid during the rolling 12-month period preceding the claim. This discrepancy is clearly addressed in both the redline and review memo.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002b: Quantifies liability cap exposure difference
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly quantifies the liability-cap gap. It calculates the draft cap at approximately $41.004 million using draft fees (or $40.392 million using the corrected APA fee table), versus an APA trailing-12-month cap of approximately $13.464 million, with a difference of about $27.540 million (or $26.928 million). These figures are in the required ballpark and demonstrate the calculation.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002c: Redlines liability cap to conform to APA Section 7.12(d)
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent replaces Section 10.1 with corrective redline language capping aggregate liability at the total Fees actually paid during the 12 months immediately preceding the date the applicable claim is first asserted in writing, with a rolling 12-month calculation thereafter. This conforms to the APA Section 7.12(d) requirement described in the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003a: Identifies non-mutual consequential damages waiver
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly identifies that draft Section 10.2 is one-sided: it waives only Polaris's claims against Trident while leaving Polaris exposed to consequential-damages claims by Trident. It also revises the provision into a mutual waiver and highlights the issue in the review memo.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003b: Redlines to make consequential damages waiver mutual
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent replaces the one-sided waiver in Section 10.2 with a mutual waiver stating that neither party is liable to the other for consequential, incidental, indirect, special, exemplary, or punitive damages.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004a: Identifies automatic renewal extending TSA beyond 18 months
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags Section 5.2’s automatic renewal as conflicting with APA §7.12(a)’s 18-month cap and recommends deleting it. Although it does not state “30 months” explicitly, it identifies that the two renewal terms could extend services beyond the APA maximum.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004b: Redlines to delete auto-renewal and impose hard 18-month stop
criteria_results.reasoning: The markup deletes the automatic-renewal provision, retains an 18-month Initial Term, and states that the TSA expires at the end of that term with no automatic renewal. Any extension requires a written amendment signed by both parties and is limited to six additional months.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005a: Identifies 120-day termination notice exceeding APA's 90 days
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags Section 5.3's 120-day notice as conflicting with APA Section 7.12(c)'s 90-day notice period, explains that 120 days exceeds the APA cap, and revises the provision to 90 days. The review memo also identifies this as a critical must-change item.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005b: Redlines termination notice to 90 days per APA
criteria_results.reasoning: The markup revises Section 5.3 from 120 days’ prior written notice to 90 days and expressly states in Seller Comment C5 that this change conforms to APA Section 7.12(c).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006a: Identifies Key Personnel consent right overriding Polaris staffing discretion
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags Section 4.3 and Schedule H as problematic because Trident's consent rights over reassignment, termination, replacements, and fixed allocations conflict with Polaris's sole staffing discretion. It replaces those provisions with seller-controlled staffing and highlights the issue in both the redline (Comment C3/C34) and review memo (S2).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006b: Proposes compromise on Key Personnel (notice + qualified replacement)
criteria_results.reasoning: Revised Section 4.3 restores Polaris's sole discretion over personnel decisions, eliminates Trident's consent right, and provides the required compromise: commercially reasonable efforts to give 15 Business Days' advance notice before replacing or reassigning a transition contact and to assign a reasonably qualified replacement.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007a: Identifies IT services 15% markup exceeding APA 10% cap
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags the IT Services 15% markup and $391,000 monthly fee as exceeding APA §7.12(b)'s 10% cap, and corrects them to 10% and $374,000 per month in Schedule B, Schedule G, and the review memo.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007b: Correctly computes IT fee difference
criteria_results.reasoning: The output correctly states that the draft IT fee of $391,000 versus the corrected $374,000 produces a $17,000 monthly overcharge and a $306,000 difference over 18 months.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007c: Notes APA compliance risk even though overcharge benefits Polaris
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly identifies the 15% IT markup as an overcharge and a violation of APA §7.12(b), labels correction to 10% as a firm must-change, and updates the monthly and total fees accordingly. This adequately recognizes the APA compliance risk despite the markup being financially favorable to Polaris.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008a: Identifies audit frequency deviation (twice/year vs. once/12 months)
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags that draft Section 14.1 permits audits twice per calendar year while the playbook limits audits to once per 12-month period, and redlines the provision to allow only one audit in any 12-month period. The review memo repeats this deviation and recommendation.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008b: Identifies audit cost allocation deviation (Seller's vs. Buyer's expense)
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags that draft Section 14.1 makes audits Seller-paid, cites the playbook requirement that audits be at Buyer's expense, and redlines the clause to state that Service Recipient may audit “at its sole expense.” The review memo likewise recommends that Buyer pay audit costs.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008c: Identifies audit notice period deviation (10 vs. 30 business days)
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags that draft Section 14.1 permits audits on 10 Business Days’ notice, contrasts this with the playbook’s 30-Business-Day requirement, and redlines the provision to require at least 30 Business Days’ prior written notice.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009a: Identifies Ohio governing law vs. playbook's Pennsylvania law
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags draft Section 15.1’s Ohio governing law as inconsistent with the playbook’s Pennsylvania-law position and proposes replacing it with Pennsylvania law. The review memo also repeats this deviation and recommendation.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009b: Identifies Cuyahoga County litigation vs. playbook's AAA arbitration in Pittsburgh
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags draft §15.2’s Cuyahoga County, Ohio court-litigation provision as inconsistent with the playbook and proposes confidential, binding arbitration under the AAA Commercial Arbitration Rules in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, following executive escalation and optional mediation.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009c: Explains strategic importance of home-state law and arbitration for Polaris
criteria_results.reasoning: The output explains the strategic rationale for Pennsylvania law and Pittsburgh arbitration: it identifies Ohio/Cuyahoga County as Trident’s home forum, notes the resulting home-court disadvantage and inconvenience for Polaris’s personnel and counsel, and states that confidential arbitration reduces discovery costs, publicity, and forum risk.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010a: Identifies overbroad perpetual IP license grant
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags Section 7.1’s perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license covering Polaris tools, methodologies, templates, software, and know-how, including modification, derivative-work, and sublicensing rights. It identifies this as a significant departure from the playbook’s firm no-license position and explains the resulting enterprise-wide proprietary IP leakage risk.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010b: Redlines to delete IP license and confirm Polaris sole ownership
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 7.1 deletes the perpetual, irrevocable license and replaces it with language confirming that all Service Provider Materials remain Polaris’s or its licensors’ sole and exclusive property. It expressly grants no license except a limited, revocable right during the TSA term to access Polaris systems solely to receive the Services, with all access ending upon termination or expiration.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011a: Identifies missing non-solicitation provision
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags the missing non-solicitation provision in the review memo (S12) and adds a new Section 7.4 restricting Trident from soliciting, recruiting, hiring, or engaging Polaris personnel who provided Services during the Term and for 12 months thereafter.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011b: Drafts non-solicitation provision with 12-month post-service tail
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 7.4 prohibits Trident from soliciting, recruiting, hiring, or engaging Polaris service personnel during the Term and for 12 months thereafter without Polaris’s prior written consent. This satisfies the required consent and 12-month post-service tail protections.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012a: Identifies CGL insurance reduction ($2M vs. $5M playbook)
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags that the draft provides only $2 million in Buyer CGL coverage compared with the playbook's $5 million target and revises Section 13.1 to require $5 million per occurrence and aggregate coverage.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012b: Identifies missing umbrella coverage requirement
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags that draft Section 13.1 omits the playbook’s $5 million umbrella/excess liability coverage requirement and proposes adding $5 million of umbrella or excess liability insurance. The review memo repeats this issue and recommendation.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012c: Identifies missing additional insured endorsement
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags that the buyer insurance provision lacks additional-insured protection and revises Section 13.1 to require Polaris to be named as an additional insured under the buyer’s CGL and umbrella/excess policies, with certificates and endorsements delivered.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_013a: Flags missing IMMEX program provisions for Monterrey facility
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly identifies the draft’s silence on IMMEX compliance for the Monterrey facility and adds Section 12.3 allocating primary responsibility to Trident for maintaining IMMEX certification and related customs, reporting, recordkeeping, and temporary-importation compliance, with limited transition assistance from Polaris. The review memo also flags this as a critical APA conformity issue.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_013b: Flags missing Mexican data privacy (LFPDPPP) provisions
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags that the draft addresses only U.S. privacy law and omits Mexico’s LFPDPPP despite processing Monterrey employees’ HR and payroll data. It proposes detailed additions covering controller/processor roles, privacy notices and consents, lawful processing, cross-border transfer mechanisms, safeguards, data-subject requests, incident notification, and deletion/return obligations.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_014a: Identifies missing termination assistance/wind-down provisions
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags the draft’s silence on termination assistance and adds a new Section 5.7 providing defined wind-down support for up to 60 days. The review memo likewise identifies the missing provision and cites the playbook’s requirement for a bounded, paid wind-down.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_014b: Proposes termination assistance at cost-plus-15% for up to 60 days
criteria_results.reasoning: The proposed new Section 5.7 expressly provides termination assistance for no more than 60 days after the affected Service ends, priced at cost-plus 15%, with defined wind-down activities.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_015a: Identifies missing change order procedure
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags the missing change order mechanism. It adds new Section 6.7 requiring a signed written change order for out-of-scope services, material volume increases, or material scope changes, and the review memo identifies the absence of such a procedure as permitting informal scope creep and unpriced expansion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_015b: Proposes change order procedure with cost-plus-15% pricing
criteria_results.reasoning: The output adds Section 6.7 requiring a written change order signed by authorized representatives of both parties for out-of-scope services, material volume increases, or material scope changes, with approved change orders and additional services priced at cost-plus 15% unless otherwise expressly agreed.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_016a: Identifies vague payment terms ('commercially reasonable time')
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags “commercially reasonable time” as vague and replaces it with a defined Net 30 payment deadline in Section 6.3. The review memo also identifies this issue and recommends Net 30 terms.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_016b: Redlines payment terms to Net 30 days
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline replaces the vague “commercially reasonable time” standard in Section 6.3 with payment of each undisputed invoice within thirty (30) days after the invoice date, which is Net 30 from invoice date.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_016c: Adds late payment interest at 1.5%/month or max legal rate
criteria_results.reasoning: Revised Section 6.3 adds late-payment interest at the lesser of 1.5% per month and the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, exactly satisfying the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_017a: Identifies missing force majeure 90-day termination trigger
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags that the draft force majeure clause lacks the playbook’s 90-day termination trigger and adds language allowing either party to terminate the affected service without penalty if the event continues for 90 consecutive days. The review memo also identifies this gap under Significant item S8.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_017b: Proposes 90-day force majeure termination right
criteria_results.reasoning: The proposed revision to Section 12.1 states that if a force majeure event continues for 90 consecutive days, either party may terminate the affected Service without penalty upon written notice.

criteria_results.title: Cover memo produced as a deliverable
criteria_results.reasoning: The output includes a seller-side review memorandum that summarizes the TSA review, including an executive summary, prioritized issues, negotiation guidance, acceptable provisions, and a conclusion. This satisfies the requirement to produce a cover memorandum.

criteria_results.title: Cover memo organizes issues by priority tiers (Critical/Significant/Minor)
criteria_results.reasoning: The cover memo expressly organizes deviations into three priority tiers: “Priority 1 — Critical / Must-Change,” “Priority 2 — Significant / Major Playbook Deviations,” and “Priority 3 — Minor / Cleanup and Negotiation Preferences.”

criteria_results.title: APA-conflict issues classified as highest priority in cover memo
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo places all specified direct APA conflicts in “Priority 1 — Critical / Must-Change”: the 200%-of-total-fees liability cap (C4), automatic renewal beyond the 18-month cap (C2), 120-day termination notice instead of 90 days (C3), and 15% IT markup exceeding the 10% cap (C6). It separately classifies playbook deviations as “Priority 2 — Significant,” clearly giving APA conflicts higher priority.

criteria_results.title: Cover memo includes negotiation strategy distinguishing firm vs. flexible positions
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo clearly distinguishes firm from flexible positions for well over three key issues. It labels the eight APA-conformity items as “Critical / Must-Change,” explains that service standard, term, notice period, fee cap, liability cap, and mutual waiver should not be traded away because they are APA-mandated, and separately identifies playbook positions as negotiable with concrete fallbacks for non-solicitation, termination assistance, payment terms, escalation, audit rights, governing law, arbitration venue, and force majeure. The stated APA conflicts and seller-risk considerations provide the required reasoning.

criteria_results.title: Redline markup includes proposed edits to the TSA
criteria_results.reasoning: The output provides a full marked-up TSA with numerous proposed deletions shown in strikethrough and additions/substitutions shown as underlined text, along with explanatory comments. It therefore includes proposed redline edits rather than merely listing issues.

criteria_results.title: Redline markup includes explanatory comments for changes
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline includes extensive explanatory seller comments tied to proposed edits. The comments identify the basis for changes—such as specific APA provisions, playbook sections, and risk-allocation positions—and generally explain the risk to Polaris and negotiation stance.

criteria_results.title: Correctly identifies Polaris as Service Provider / Seller throughout
criteria_results.reasoning: The output consistently identifies Polaris Industrial Holdings, Inc. as the Seller and Service Provider and Trident as the Buyer and Service Recipient. The redline, comments, and review memorandum are framed from Polaris’s seller-side perspective and recommend protections for Polaris as the service provider, without material party-role confusion.

criteria_results.title: References APA Section 7.12 when flagging APA-conflict issues
criteria_results.reasoning: The output repeatedly cites APA Section 7.12 and relevant subsections when flagging the specified APA conflicts: §7.12(a) for term/renewal, §7.12(c) for termination notice, §7.12(b) for fee markup and adjustments, and §7.12(d) for the liability cap and consequential-damages waiver.

criteria_results.title: Fee escalation provision addressed (playbook: greater of 3% or CPI-U)
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly addresses fee escalation in revised Section 6.4, proposing annual adjustments by the greater of 3% or the trailing 12-month CPI-U increase. It also identifies this as the Playbook §4.2 position in both the redline comment and review memo.

criteria_results.title: Indemnification provision addressed (Buyer indemnifies for third-party claims)
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly addresses indemnification in revised Section 9.1 and the review memo. It provides that the Buyer/Service Recipient indemnifies the Seller for third-party claims arising from the Buyer’s operation of the business and use of or reliance on the services, except to the extent caused by the Seller’s gross negligence, fraud, or willful misconduct, consistent with the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Both deliverable files are produced
criteria_results.reasoning: The output includes two distinct, clearly identified deliverables: (1) “tsa-markup-redline.docx,” containing the seller’s redlined and annotated TSA, and (2) “tsa-review-memo.docx,” containing a separate seller-side cover memorandum to the partner.

criteria_results.title: Correct total monthly service cost baseline ($1,020,000) referenced
criteria_results.reasoning: The output correctly references both aggregate baselines: Schedule G lists total base monthly cost of $1,020,000 and the corrected total monthly fee at a 10% markup of $1,122,000. The review memo also repeatedly uses the $1.122 million monthly fee figure in its calculations.

criteria_results.title: Playbook's dispute escalation to senior executives referenced
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly adds Section 15.2 requiring disputes to be escalated first to the parties’ designated CFO or General Counsel representatives, with 15 Business Days to resolve the dispute before mediation or AAA arbitration. The review memo also references executive escalation before arbitration.

criteria_results.title: Redline comments explain specific risk to Polaris for at least five changes
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline includes well over five distinct comments identifying concrete risks to Polaris. Examples include unpriced scope and compliance exposure (C1), an undefined higher service standard (C2), workforce-management burdens from personnel lockups (C3), involuntary service extensions and fixed pricing (C4), permanent leakage of enterprise IP (C9), Mexican data-law compliance risk (C10), quantified excess liability exposure of approximately $27.54 million (C13), and disruption and proprietary-system exposure from broad audits (C18). These go beyond mechanical APA or playbook citations and explain specific adverse consequences.
